name: Angular
shortDescription: Angular helps you build a web app from smaller page parts. Learn to show data, use buttons and move between pages. Start after HTML and JavaScript.
highlights: Show data and handle button clicks
Add forms and move between pages

name: React
shortDescription: React helps you build a web page from small parts called components. Learn to pass data to a part and change the page when someone clicks.
highlights: Update the page after a click

name: Vue.js
shortDescription: Vue builds a page from small parts called components. It connects values to the page and updates the page when those values change. Start with a greeting, then add choices, lists and a little memory.
highlights: Practise connect an input with v-model
Practise leave a slot for content

name: Svelte
shortDescription: Svelte builds interactive pages from small component files. Its compiler prepares those files for the browser. Learn values, buttons and lists with Svelte 5 runes, one small example at a time.
highlights: Practise run and clean up an effect

name: Next.js
shortDescription: Next.js adds page routing and build tools to React. This course uses a small site that can be exported as static files. Learn page files, shared layouts and browser interactions without adding a login or database.
highlights: Practise generate a small set of book pages

name: Nuxt.js
shortDescription: Nuxt adds page routing and project tools to Vue. This starter course builds a small site from pages and shared layouts. It uses local content and a static build, so the finished sample does not need a login or a database.
highlights: Practise run browser-only work after mount

name: Remix
shortDescription: Remix ideas now live in React Router's framework tools. This course teaches routes, nested pages and browser data loading in a small single-page app. It uses local data and avoids a runtime server.
highlights: Practise use search values in the address

name: Astro
shortDescription: Astro makes content pages with very little browser JavaScript by default. It can add interactive parts only where needed. Learn pages, layouts and small content lists before adding an optional interactive island.
highlights: Practise make a list at build time

name: jQuery
shortDescription: jQuery is a JavaScript library used by many existing websites. It gives short tools for selecting page parts and handling events. Learn what those tools do, then see how similar jobs work with the browser DOM.

name: Redux
shortDescription: Redux keeps shared app state in one store. Actions describe changes, and reducers decide the next state. This course uses Redux Toolkit to make those rules short and clear, with tiny counters and reading lists.
highlights: Practise name a slice of state
Practise read and dispatch from react

name: NgRx
shortDescription: NgRx helps Angular apps organise shared state. Actions say what happened, reducers choose the next values, and selectors read them. Learn each part with a small reading counter before meeting effects and SignalStore.
highlights: Practise put a value in an action
Practise use a store value as a signal

name: RxJS
shortDescription: RxJS works with values that arrive over time. An observable is a stream of those values. Operators can change, filter or combine streams. Learn with small number streams before using clicks and waiting tasks.
highlights: Practise turn clicks into a stream

name: Zustand
shortDescription: Zustand keeps small shared state stores for JavaScript and React. A store can hold values and actions that change them. Learn a counter, a reading list and careful browser saving without creating an account.

name: React Native
shortDescription: React Native uses React ideas to build mobile app screens. Its View and Text components are different from web HTML. Learn a small screen, clear controls and a reading list using core mobile components.
highlights: Practise scroll a small amount of content
Practise respect the safe screen area

name: Ionic
shortDescription: Ionic provides web components styled for app screens. With React, you can build pages, lists and forms that work in a browser and can be packaged for devices. Start with the browser version and simple local state.
highlights: Practise open and close a modal

name: Electron
shortDescription: Electron packages web pages as a desktop app. It has a main process for app windows and a renderer for the page. Learn a small local window and a narrow, safe bridge between the two sides.

name: Three.js
shortDescription: Three.js helps JavaScript draw 3D scenes in a browser. A scene holds objects, a camera chooses the view and a renderer draws the picture. Learn one cube before adding movement, light and cleanup.

name: D3.js
shortDescription: D3 connects data to page elements. It can choose positions, colours and labels to make a chart. Learn a few SVG shapes, then connect a small list of numbers to a bar chart you can explain.
highlights: Practise put data into a join

name: Chart.js
shortDescription: Chart.js draws charts on a canvas. You supply labels, values and a few options. Learn how to choose a clear chart, label its numbers and update it without hiding the data from readers.

name: GSAP
shortDescription: GSAP animates values over time. You can move a page part, fade it in or arrange several steps on a timeline. Learn clear, small movements and respect people who prefer less motion.
highlights: Practise start from a chosen value
Practise sequence steps on a timeline
